# Digs Raises $25.3M in Series A Funding
...
August 27, 2026
...
Digs, a Vancouver, Washington-based artificial intelligence and digital twin platform for the residential construction industry, raised $25.3m in Series A funding.
...
The investment, which brought total funding to more than $47m, was made by Builders FirstSource.
...
The company will use the capital to extend its workforce to over 60, focusing hiring efforts across its core product engineering, architectural design, and software development teams while scaling its national sales presence.
...
Co-founded in 2022 by CEO Ryan Fink and Ty Frackiewicz, Digs develops an AI-powered collaboration platform and residential construction workspace designed to generate an interactive digital twin of a home that persists throughout its entire lifecycle.
...
Operating under a five-year enterprise deal, Builders FirstSource will integrate Digs’ SaaS technology directly into its digital ecosystem to serve over 140,000 professional homebuilders.

...
Digs is receiving two forms of leverage from Builders FirstSource at once. The Vancouver, Washington construction-software company announced a $25.3M Series A led solely by Builders FirstSource, alongside a five-year commercial agreement that connects investment capital with product and distribution work.
...
Builders FirstSource is the solo lead investor in Digs' $25.3M Series A, announced on August 25, 2026. The companies also entered a five-year commercial agreement intended to accelerate product development, deepen platform integration, and expand AI capabilities across pre-construction, procurement, construction, homeowner handoff, warranty, and aftercare.
...
Digs' financing history requires careful arithmetic because earlier announcements used different round labels. The company came out of stealth with a $7M pre-seed in 2023, then raised a $7M Seed in January 2024 led by Oregon Venture Fund and Legacy Capital Ventures. An additional $5M financing announced in November 2025 brought pre-Series A funding to nearly $20M.

# Homebuilding AI startup Digs raises $25.3M, led by Builders FirstSource

What's the deal? Digs, a Vancouver, Washington-based startup building AI software for residential construction, raised $25.3 million in Series A funding led by building products giant Builders FirstSource Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom →. The companies announced the round, alongside a five-year partnership, on August 25, 2026.

What's the endgame? Under the agreement, Builders FirstSource will integrate Digs' AI platform into its digital ecosystem, expanding tools for its 140,000 builder clients. The technology handles pre-construction estimates, blueprint collaboration, and post-move-in maintenance and warranty care.

The details: Founded in 2022 by Ryan Fink and Ty Frackiewicz, Digs charges builders on a SaaS model and has thousands of homes on its platform across all 50 states. The round pushes its total funding past $47 million, building on a $5 million pre-Series A last year. Earlier backers include Fuse, Flying Fish Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom →, Oregon Venture Fund Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom →, and Cascade Seed Fund Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom →.

What's the money for? Digs has grown to 37 employees and plans to more than double that to over 60 by the end of the year, mostly in engineering, design, and product. Fink describes the tool as a "CarFax for the home," replacing static PDF blueprints with an AI hub that tracks a property's history, materials, and warranty details.

Why now? Fink said the partnership moves Digs closer to its vision of building "the first scalable true digital twin of the home" that outlives the construction phase. Builders FirstSource, the nation's largest supplier of building materials, operates roughly 565 locations across 43 states and serves 91 of the top 100 US metropolitan markets.

The backer's view: "Our customers are looking for seamless technology that helps them operate more efficiently and deliver a better homeowner experience," Builders FirstSource president and chief executive officer Peter Jackson said in a statement.

The signal: At $25.3 million, the round lands in roughly the 91st percentile of all US enterprise software Series A deals on record — a sizeable bet on AI reaching one of construction's most paperwork-heavy corners. Backing from a Fortune 500 customer, rather than a traditional venture firm, signals how incumbents are moving to own the software layer of homebuilding.
